## Database schema changes

Migration version 2 creates STRICT normalized tables for `hosts`, `services`, `service_ports`, `service_paths`, and `service_dependencies`, plus supporting indexes. It adds checked enums and port ranges, nonblank path requirements, per-parent child ID and position uniqueness, dependency uniqueness/self-reference protection, foreign keys, per-record revisions, timestamps on primary inventory records, and `application_metadata.inventory_revision`.

The migration checksum covers both the complete DDL and inventory-revision metadata initialization.

## Migration behavior from Task 1

A Task 1 database migrates forward transactionally from schema version 1 to version 2. Existing `installation_id` and `created_at` metadata remain unchanged. The new inventory tables begin empty and inventory revision begins at zero. A failed migration rolls back all schema and metadata changes and is not recorded. Existing checksum validation, altered-migration rejection, and unsupported-future-version rejection remain in place.

## Repository and transaction behavior

Host and service CRUD is synchronous and typed. Every create, update, or delete runs in a better-sqlite3 transaction and increments the application inventory revision exactly once. Service create/update writes the parent, ports, paths, and dependencies atomically; any validation, uniqueness, or foreign-key failure rolls back the complete mutation. Reads return deterministic host/service ordering and stored child/dependency ordering.

## Foreign-key and delete behavior

- Services may reference an existing host; host deletion is restricted while referenced.
- Ports and paths cascade when their service is deleted.
- Outgoing and incoming dependency links cascade when either referenced service is deleted.
- Dependent services whose dependency is deleted receive a new revision and updated timestamp.
- Invalid host or dependency references fail transactionally.

## Optimistic concurrency

Hosts and services start at revision 1. Updates and deletes require an expected positive integer revision and atomically match it in SQL. Successful updates increment the record revision. Stale revisions raise `InventoryConflictError`; missing records raise `InventoryNotFoundError`; failed mutations do not increment the global inventory revision. Invalid or corrupted inventory-revision metadata fails closed.

## Data safety and datastore authority

No IndexedDB data is read, changed, migrated, overwritten, or deleted. No production inventory is copied to SQLite. The migration only creates empty server-side inventory structures and preserves Task 1 metadata. IndexedDB remains the sole authoritative datastore for all production inventory throughout Task 2.
